extracted.intended_audience: news editors, war correspondents and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service news dispatches reporting Allied and Soviet wartime operations, casualties, press schedules and human-interest battlefield vignettes. Focus is on timely, attributed facts (troop movements, losses, air raids) with occasional feature/eyewitness material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casualty reporting (broken down by killed/wounded/missing and nationality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report totals of killed, wounded and missing and break them down by nationality (e.g., United States casualties were 11,156 killed, 52,710 wounded and 6,143 missing; British losses were 5,646 killed, 27,766 wounded and 6,182 missing; Canadian casualties were 919 killed, 4,354 wounded and 1,272 missing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the time span covered (e.g., 'from D day, June 6, through July 20'), note inclusion of related incidents (e.g., 'Included in these figures were the casualties sustained during pre-invasion exercises last April'), and where available include interpretive percentages (e.g., 'Of all casualties ... about 3 per cent have been fatal' and comparisons like 'Allied casualties ... had been 30 per cent under the anticipated figure'). Attribute figures to the announcing authority (e.g., 'Supreme Headquarters announced').

rubrics_metrics.name: Press communique and conference schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the official schedule and procedures for press communiques and conferences (e.g., 'henceforth there would be only one formal communique daily, to be issued at 5 A. M. (Eastern wartime).' A half-hour press communique given at a press conference, feature material at 10:15 A.M., and formal conferences at 11 A.M. and 5 P.M.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reasons for the schedule (e.g., 'the extra work involved in greatly expanded operations made it impractical to issue twice-daily communiques') and note practical details reporters must follow (timing, expected length and focus of each session).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official sources and named officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute operational claims, casualty figures, percentages and medical or logistic claims to an authoritative source (e.g., 'Supreme Headquarters announced', 'Maj Gen. A. W. Kenner, chief of the Medical Corps', 'Gen. Eisenhower’s Command').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named sources for figures and assessments, indicate organizational affiliation (e.g., 'Supreme Headquarters, Allied Expeditionary Force'), and distinguish official communiques from correspondent reports or eyewitness accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational reporting of troop movements and territorial gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Report unit advances, towns captured, river crossings and proximity to strategic objectives with geographic specifics (e.g., 'American units ... driving southward across Brittany, have reached a point several miles south of St. Gildas des Bois, which is eighteen miles from St. Nazaire'; 'crossed the Mayenne River, two miles south of Mayenne').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include distances, directions, unit names where available, contextual strategic significance (e.g., threat of being outflanked, pocket formations), and note uncertainty or lack of Allied substantiation when reporting enemy claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature/eyewitness human-interest material
rubrics_metrics.description: Include vivid on-the-scene anecdotes and eyewitness details that illustrate civilian reaction or battlefield human drama (e.g., crowds cheering entry of liberating troops, French collaborationists being seized and paraded, account of rescue of downed pilots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place feature material in separate segments or designated press sessions (the dispatch notes a separate conference 'mainly devoted to feature material'), use firsthand quotes and descriptive detail, and clarify source or delay if report is 'delayed' from location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air operations and bombing mission reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mission specifics for air raids: numbers and types of aircraft, targets hit, claimed effects (direct hits on submarine pens, oil refineries, factories), fighter escort actions and losses (e.g., 'more than 1,100 American Flying Fortresses and Liberators ... 29 German fighters destroyed ... Thirteen American heavy bombers and six fighters were lost').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report purpose of missions (e.g., 'Designed To Trap Enemy Subs'), results visible on reconnaissance or photographic evidence (e.g., 'air photographs showed that at least three direct hits were scored'), and losses on both sides. Attribute claims to returning airmen or official air force communiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative analysis and percentage interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use comparative statistics and percentages to interpret raw numbers (e.g., 'this would indicate that Americans composed 60 per cent of the forces in France', 'Allied casualties ... had been 30 per cent under the anticipated figure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how ratios or percentages were derived when asserting proportional strength or deviation from expected casualties, and indicate source of expectations or baselines where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful use of military terminology and operational context
rubrics_metrics.description: Use accurate military terminology and refer to established defensive systems and geographic features correctly (e.g., 'Maginot line', 'Siegfried lines', 'Orne River valley', 'Vire', 'Loire-Seine triangle').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating breakthroughs; report both the tactical picture and broader strategic cautions (e.g., 'This does not mean that the high­way to Paris is open ... there is plenty of room in the Loire-Seine triangle for a strong German stand'). Clarify when claims come from enemy propaganda versus reconnaissance.
